rv.q: Leavitt has written a seriously comic gem, one that earns every laugh while quietly preparing the ground for moments of genuine emotional force.
Sukkot is very well worth the watching.
Sukkot at 59E59 to emerge as that rare, lovely beast, a dysfunctional family dramedy that feels both fresh and believable.
Sukkot is a seriously comic gem.

There is plenty here to admire: four terrific performances, a beautiful production, characters who are unique yet recognizable, and a story willing to examine grief, family roles, resentment, tradition and the complicated ways we love the people closest to us.
Overall, I rarely found it moving.

cn.t: Critics praise this satisfying family comedy-drama about grief and connection, with a widower building a sukkah to honor his late Jewish wife. The deceptively simple premise yields an emotionally resonant exploration of loss and healing.
